author: Mithali Dorai Raj
prose_text_en: Mithali Dorai Raj, born in Hyderabad with Tamil as her mother tongue, is a legendary Indian cricketer. She began playing at 10 and was selected for the national team at 17. She is the first female cricketer to surpass 6,000 runs in ODIs and the first to score seven consecutive 50s. Known as the 'Tendulkar of Indian women’s cricket,' Mithali has often expressed that while comparisons to Sachin are a privilege, she prefers an individual identity. She received the Padma Shri for her contributions. Another featured sportsperson, Usha Rani, a Karnataka police officer, rose from the shanty town of Subedarpalaya to become a national-level Kabaddi champion.
summary_en: This lesson highlights the achievements and struggles of Indian female sports icons, Mithali Raj and Usha Rani. It emphasizes how both players overcame societal barriers and personal challenges to excel in their respective fields of cricket and kabaddi. The text serves as an inspiration, encouraging readers to break gender stereotypes and pursue their passions.
